newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk Aksigorta aims to double 97 premiums.
newsitem.headline: Turk Aksigorta aims to double 97 premiums.

text.p: Turkey's leading insurer Aksigorta A.S. aims to raise its total premium revenue by almost 100 percent to more than 17.5 trillion lira ($114 million) in 1997, a senior company official said.

"Every year, our aim is to increase premiums by 15 percent in real terms, but this rate will be exceeded this year. We expect our premium revenue to be more than 17.5 trillion lira," Sami Vodina, assistant general manager of Aksigorta told Reuters.
Turkey's end-1997 inflation is expected to be at around 75-80 percent, according to official forecasts.

Aksigorta shares closed at 9,600 lira on the Istanbul stock exchange on Wednesday, up from 9,100 lira on Tuesday. The market index dropped 1.33 percent to 2,009 in consolidation of the recent sharp gains.
"Our 1997 growth is more than the previous years because we are expanding our sales organisation. We follow a policy of reaching out to the customer," Vodina said.

He added that new regional offices were opened in the towns Diyarbakir, Trabzon, Denizli towns and representative offices in the cities of Istanbul, Eskisehir and Antalya. "Our aim in opening the new offices was to be closer to the clients. As a result, the rise in our premiums was above previous expectations," Vodina said.
In 1996, Aksigorta had a total direct premium revenue of 8.9 trillion lira, up from 4.6 trillion lira in 1995.
The company reported a net profit of 1.71 trillion lira in 1996, up sharply from 651.6 billion a year ago.
"Our policy of expanding our sales organisation will be in effect until the year 2000. We also invested $3 million in data processing to establish on-line links with our agencies," Vodina said.
He added that more than 100 agencies were currently linked up, out of 1,260 spread throughout Turkey.
Aksigorta is largely owned by Sabanci Holding, one of Turkey's leading industrial conglomerates which recently floated part of its capital.
The company also uses 484 branches of Akbank, Sabanci's banking arm and one of Turkey's leading commercial banks, as agents.
Vodina said a new project to further expand on-line links with agencies would be developed soon. "I do not expect this investment to be below $7 million," he added.
